subject: Dedicated sizing for CedarBend pilot: tokens/sec, latency & headroom
messages:
From: Jaspreet Singh <ops@cedarbend.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial traffic & latency goals for Dedicated pilot

Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To put the ask in writing so we can get a sizing recommendation:

- Pilot window: 30 days (production mirror) followed by month-1 commitment discussions.
- Target model: redwood/red-7b-quant (we'll confirm exact variant once you send quant recommendations).
- Typical request shape (from our prod sample): median payload ~ 600 tokens, median response ~ 450 tokens.
- Expected sustained TPS (tokens/sec): ~9,000 tokens/sec across the fleet during our daytime peak (US PST).
- Burst tolerance: up to 2x sustained for short windows (5–15 minutes) during product launches.
- P95 latency target: <= 300ms for generation API (end-to-end as measured at our edge).

Attached is a small sample of our traffic (prod_traffic_sample.csv). Can your team provide a recommended Dedicated slab configuration (GPU count/sku), suggested headroom for the SLOs, and a short canary plan so we can validate before full commit? Also please include notes on prefix/KV caching assumptions and whether a small quantized variant materially lowers GPU need.

Procurement is watching timelines — we'd like a ballpark estimate for sustained + burst capacity by EOD Friday if possible so internal approvals can start.

Best,
Jaspreet Singh
Head of Platform | CedarBend Health

--
Attachment: prod_traffic_sample.csv (3.2KB stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jaspreet Singh <ops@cedarbend.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic & latency goals for Dedicated pilot

Jaspreet — thanks for the detail and the sample. Looping in Ben (SE) and Kim (Solutions) for the technical sizing and canary plan. Preliminary read below — sending a short spreadsheet with assumptions shortly (cedarbend_prelim_sizing.xlsx).

Quick high-level estimate (preliminary):
- Model/shape assumptions: redwood/red-7b-quant at 0.5x runtime tokens-per-op vs fp16; median response size matches your sample.
- Sustained capacity: estimated need ~6x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs to meet ~9k tokens/sec with p95 ~250–320ms depending on KV cache hit rate.
- Burst pool: recommend an additional 2x GPUs reserved for 2x bursts (gives ~2x sustained for short periods for your pattern).
- Headroom: request +25–30% capacity margin on top of sustained to keep on-box queuing low and absorb cold starts; if you enable aggressive prefix/KV caching we can shrink sustained by ~1 GPU equivalency.

Caveats and immediate asks:
- Need to confirm model variant and whether you will accept a quantized 4-bit variant in pilot. Quantization typically reduces memory footprint and effective GPU cost but can increase p95 a bit on tail cases — we'll quantify in the sizing doc.
- Please confirm expected concurrency per second (distinct requests) vs token throughput if possible; sample hints at ~18 reqs/sec at peak.

Next steps I propose:
1) We'll send the preliminary sizing workbook (attached).
2) Ben will provide a short latency-vs-GPU curve and a canary checklist by EOD.
3) We’ll propose a 48–72 hour canary plan with traffic mirroring and a smoke SLA (p95 <= 350ms) before committing to the full reserved slab.

I'll keep procurement in the loop once we land on the final GPU counts.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: cedarbend_prelim_sizing.xlsx (11KB stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jaspreet Singh <ops@cedarbend.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T12:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic & latency goals for Dedicated pilot

Thanks Marissa — adding a few engineering specifics from the SE side.

Short technical notes (for sizing workbook):
- Baseline: redwood/red-7b-quant on A100-80GB equiv yields ~1.6k–1.8k tokens/sec sustained per GPU at p95 ~280ms under your median reply size (no KV cache). With a warmed KV cache and prefix caching we commonly see 30–45% effective throughput uplift.
- Recommendation: size for conservative steady-state at 1.5k tokens/sec/GPU -> 9k / 1.5k -> 6 GPUs (sustained). Add 2 GPUs as a dedicated burst/hedge pool that can be pre-warmed and routed during launches.
- Autoscaling/burst handling: we recommend routing policy that prefers dedicated slab first, then burst pool, with a fallback to hosted tier (if enabled) under sustained overload to protect p95.
- Canary checklist: mirror 5% of production traffic for 48 hours, validate KV hit rates, measure tail latency (p99) and cold-starts, confirm quantized variant quality on 1k eval prompts.

Procurement/ops asks:
- If CedarBend needs the 2x burst to be contractual (reserved), we'll surface pricing delta. If burst can be shared on a best-effort pool, cost is lower but less isolation.

I attached the internal playbook that outlines default network/cold-start mitigations and our typical SLA-exception flow.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: redwood_capacity_playbook.pdf (240KB stub)

From: Jaspreet Singh <ops@cedarbend.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@cedarbend.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T14:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic & latency goals for Dedicated pilot

Marissa / Ben —

This looks sensible and aligned with our internal expectations. A few confirmations:
1) We accept the preliminary split: 6 sustained GPUs + 2 burst GPUs (either physically reserved or warmed shared pool — procurement prefers reserved for guaranteed launches; ops prefers shared for cost). Can you outline both pricing/contract differences?
2) Canary: we’ll do the 48h mirror at ~5% traffic starting Oct 4th. Need a short statement of expected metrics to pass (p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms, no more than 3% 5xxs).
3) Quantization: we’re open to 4-bit for pilot if you provide the 1k-eval-quality report and confirm inference latency tradeoffs.

Procurement — please hold off on formal PO until we get the sizing + price delta. Marissa, if you can provide an updated workbook with two pricing lines (reserved-burst vs shared-burst) and a one-page canary acceptance criteria doc, that will let us schedule internal approvals.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’ll aim to finalize by next week.

Thanks,
Jaspreet Singh
Head of Platform | CedarBend Health
